thread:
anya: quick check-in on the ‘slot coherence’ refactor — sketch attached below. want to validate tradeoffs before i write the rfc.

sam: +1. curious about how you plan to handle headroom signaling across slots. that was a pain last time.

anya: right — thinking of explicit per-slot headroom tokens emitted by the admission controller. cheap to check, avoids global locks.

mike: tokens are fine but how do we prevent token hogging from bursty tenants?

anya: combine tokens with a soft depletion rate per-tenant and a short-lived reclaim window. basically: if tenant uses > burst_quota in last 1s, start probabilistic drop.

rachael: sounds like rate-limiter + eviction hint. can you paste the pseudocode?

anya: sure:
```
# admission pseudocode
if tenant.headroom_tokens > 0:
  grant_slot(tenant)
  tenant.headroom_tokens -= 1
else:
  if tenant.recent_usage < burst_threshold:
    queue_in_slot(tenant)
  else:
    mark_for_reclaim(tenant)
```

sam: where do kv-cache eviction signals fit? we need slots to carry deadline hints so the kvcache can bias evictions away from soon-to-complete slots.

anya: exactly — slot metadata includes deadline_hint, kv_score_weight. when slot is aged > x ms we lower kv_score_weight to make it evictable.

mike: sounds plausible. what about fairness across slots with mixed seq-lens? long-context tenants will always anchor big windows and get more batched tokens.

anya: plan is to normalize by weighted_token_budget: tokens_per_slot = slot.size * (1 / tenant.normalized_priority). gives smaller tenants fewer tokens but prevents long-context from starving.

rachael: how do we set normalized_priority? static account tier? runtime feedback?

anya: runtime feedback + initial tier hint. adjust every minute based on realized latency SLO misses and throughput.

sam: runtime feedback loop seems tricky — need to avoid oscillation. add a dampening factor and hysteresis. also, ensure metric windows are long enough for signal.

anya: agreed. plan: exponential moving avg with alpha=0.2, apply +10% cap per update.

infra-bot: deploy: batcher/refactor/slot-coherence v0.1 -> canary started (sha: d3f9a1). :rocket:

mike: canary? nice. any safety fallback if headroom tokens miscomputed?

anya: fallback: revert to legacy global-admission path for that tenant if token error rate > 0.5% in 30s. also metrics: token_grant_mismatch and slot_starved_count.

rachael: do we have observability hooks for slot lifecycle? need traces: slot.create, slot.dispatch, slot.evict with tenant, deadline_hint.

anya: yes — proto events added. small payload to avoid cardinality explosion: only tenant_id hash and qualitative signal (low/med/high).

sam: thumbs up. last ask: include a short sim run in the rfc with 1000 tenants, mixed seq-dist, and a couple of failure modes (kvcache eviction thrash, bursty tenant overload).

anya: will do. adding a section on tradeoffs: simplicity vs optimal packing; deterministic fairness vs dynamic responsiveness; per-slot metadata cost vs eviction quality.

mike: love it. keep the doc pragmatic. minimal global state.

anya: ok will draft rfc this afternoon and ping here for review. :+1:
